Answer: B
Reason: The CT image (Figure 2b) shows a heavily calcified, stenotic lesion in the right pulmonary artery (indicated by the arrow), which is characteristic of chronic vascular inflammation and fibrosis seen in Takayasu arteritis rather than an acute thromboembolism. This chronic obstruction explains the patient's symptoms of shortness of breath and chest pain during the increased hemodynamic demands of pregnancy.
